candidates.attacker_control: The XML string is fully attacker-controlled on two unauthenticated paths handled by SingleSignOutHandler.process() when the SingleSignOutFilter (or Tomcat SingleSignOutValve) is deployed: (1) front-channel logout: GET request parameter SAMLRequest (default name, setFrontLogoutParameterName), base64+raw-deflate decoded in uncompressLogoutMessage() and passed to XmlUtils.getTextForElement(); (2) back-channel logout: POST request parameter logoutRequest, likewise passed to XmlUtils.getTextForElement(). Neither path authenticates the sender or verifies a signature/source, so any HTTP client can supply arbitrary XML (including a DOCTYPE with SYSTEM entities).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that load-external-dtd is already disabled (this blocks the classic 'SYSTEM "..."' external DTD subset payload but not entities declared in the internal subset and not explicitly disabled external-general/parameter-entities features). Checked that SingleSignOutHandler only uses the parsed text as a lookup key (no reflection of file contents in the HTTP response), which limits impact to blind/OOB scenarios. Checked that isBackChannelLogoutRequest requires POST and rejects multipart, and that safeGetParameter constrains which requests reach the parser, but neither adds authentication or XML hardening. Checked the same pattern in Cas20ServiceTicketValidator.extractCustomAttributes (raw SAXParserFactory, no hardening) but its input is the CAS server response, i.e. trusted-side, so it is not counted separately (same root weakness, weaker attacker control).
candidates.impact: Blind XML External Entity injection in the application server process: disclosure of local files/URLs reachable by the JVM where an out-of-band channel is available, server-side request forgery against internal or external hosts, and parser/entity-based denial of service. The parsed value is used as a session-mapping key (removeSessionByMappingId) rather than echoed to the caller, so the primary realistic impacts are SSRF/blind data exfiltration and DoS rather than direct reflected file disclosure.
candidates.prerequisites: SingleSignOutFilter/SingleSignOutHandler (or the Tomcat SingleSignOutValve) must be configured, which is the normal way to enable CAS single sign-out; the attacker needs only ordinary network access to the application; no ticket, session or credential is required. Exploitation of the entity step depends on the JAXP/Xerces version resolving external general entities declared in the internal DTD subset while load-external-dtd=false is set (the code does not disable them, which is the standard recommended mitigation).
candidates.root_cause: XmlUtils.getXmlReader() (cas-client-core/src/main/java/org/jasig/cas/client/util/XmlUtils.java:53-63) creates the SAX reader from SAXParserFactory.newInstance() and only sets: namespaces=true, namespace-prefixes=false and 'http://apache.org/xml/features/nonvalidating/load-external-dtd'=false. It does not set 'http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl'=true nor 'http://xml.org/sax/features/external-general-entities'=false nor 'http://xml.org/sax/features/external-parameter-entities'=false. Disabling only the external DTD subset does not stop external entities declared inline in a document's internal DTD subset (a well-known Xerces partial mitigation), so a DOCTYPE with '<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///...">' referenced in the document can still be resolved by the parser.
candidates.title: Incomplete XXE hardening in XmlUtils allows external entity expansion on attacker-controllable Single-Sign-Out XML (SAMLRequest/logoutRequest)
candidates.trace: Anonymous HTTP GET/POST -> ServletRequest params SAMLRequest / logoutRequest -> SingleSignOutHandler.isFrontChannelLogoutRequest()/isBackChannelLogoutRequest() (lines 171-188) -> destroySession() (line 284) -> SafeGetParameter -> uncompressLogoutMessage() (line 255) for front-channel -> XmlUtils.getTextForElement(logoutMessage, "SessionIndex") (line 295) -> XmlUtils.getXmlReader() (line 53) builds the SAX parser -> SAX parser parses attacker XML with external general entities still enabled -> external entity (e.g., file:// or http://) is dereferenced by the server while processing the request.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed: whether the deployed JAXP/Xerces version actually resolves internal-subset external general entities with load-external-dtd=false was not executed or tested; the source alone shows the entity-hardening features are absent. No proof of a working OOB exfiltration channel or of file contents being observable to the attacker. Some call paths (Saml11TicketValidator/BasicParserPool, proxy validators) were not exhaustively analysed for parser configuration.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-611 Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference (XXE)

coverage_summary: Scope: 155 model-visible files of 156 under the assigned root (one file filtered by the sensitive-name/path policy; binary-like files are skipped by the readers). The P1 relation index covers 135 parsed Java files with 1,202 symbols and 2,008 syntax edges but explicitly implements no control flow/data flow/semantic resolution (2,186 unresolved calls), so it was used only for navigation. I read the cas-client-core main sources in full for the security-relevant components (authentication filters and redirect strategies, validation filters/validators incl. SAML and proxy validators, SingleSignOutHandler/Filter and session mapping storage, proxy/GrantingTicket storage and retriever, CommonUtils/XmlUtils/config filters, SSL hostname verifiers and HTTPS factory, JAAS CasLoginModule and callback/filters) plus the Tomcat common/v6/v7 authenticators, valves, realms and the JBoss/Atlassian authenticator entry points; unit tests were consulted where they document intended behaviour. Not exhaustively line-reviewed: large third-party-facing build files (Atlassian pom with hundreds of dependency exclusions), thin Tomcat v7 subclasses not individually read (they mirror the v6 classes read), and the excluded sensitive-named file. No runtime, build, test or exploit execution was performed.
limitations: No code execution/runtime verification; the XXE candidate depends on JAXP/Xerces behaviour (internal-subset external entity resolution with load-external-dtd=false) that was reasoned from source and hardening guidance, not executed.

P1 relation index is partial: no data-flow/control-flow/semantic resolution; 2,186 unresolved calls and 13 omitted files, so cross-file flow claims (e.g. all callers of XmlUtils) rely on manual text search, which is not guaranteed complete.
One repository file was excluded by the sensitive-name/path filter and could not be inspected; binary-like files are skipped.

Impact of the XXE candidate is limited because the parsed text is used as a session-mapping key and is not returned to the caller, so only blind/OOB disclosure, SSRF and DoS are supported; a working out-of-band channel was not demonstrated.
Tomcat v7 wrappers and Atlassian integration were only inspected at entry points; their container-specific session/auth behaviour could not be exercised.
Module build configurations were read for versions/context only; dependency-level issues (e.g. OpenSAML BasicParserPool defaults) were not resolved or tested.

rejected_leads.lead: AuthenticationFilter.isRequestUrlExcluded() builds the match target from request.getRequestURL() plus the raw query string, so a loose ignorePattern can be satisfied by appending a query string (auth bypass of the redirect filter). Rejected as a submitted candidate: impact depends entirely on an administrator-supplied ignorePattern (patterns matching path prefixes or anchored regexes are unaffected), it is a hardening/design concern rather than clearly incorrect code, and no source evidence of a fix or an unconditional bypass exists.
rejected_leads.reason: Config-dependent, requires a loose administrator-chosen pattern; not attacker-exploitable for default/anchored configurations.

rejected_leads.lead: CommonUtils.findMatchingServerName() compares the Host header with '==' (host == "localhost", line 219) instead of equals, so X-Forwarded-Host is effectively never consulted. Rejected: the function only selects among administrator-configured serverName values (or returns serverNames[0]); the branch is also skipped entirely when a single server name is configured, so no attacker-controlled host is ever introduced into the constructed service URL.
rejected_leads.reason: Functional string-comparison bug with no demonstrated attacker-controlled security impact; service URL still uses configured server names.

rejected_leads.lead: SingleSignOutHandler destroys sessions for unauthenticated logoutRequest/SAMLRequest messages (no signature or source check), and recordSession() lets any caller bind an arbitrary token to their own session. Rejected as the primary candidate: to log out another user the attacker must know the victim's CAS SessionIndex (server-generated opaque value not exposed by the client paths reviewed), reducing this to a conditional DoS with weaker evidence than the XML issue; no session-hijack primitive was traced.
rejected_leads.reason: Requires knowledge of an opaque SessionIndex; primary effect is conditional session-logout DoS.

rejected_leads.lead: CasLoginModule.cleanCache() uses assertion.getValidFromDate() instead of getValidUntilDate(), so cached assertions are not purged based on their validity end. Rejected: it still removes entries older than cacheTimeout (effectively creation-time based), requires cacheAssertions=true plus JAAS deployment, and reuse of a cached assertion is keyed by the one-time ticket string, so no clear privilege escalation was traced.
rejected_leads.reason: Weak impact, configuration-gated, and not clearly exploitable.

rejected_leads.lead: AbstractUrlBasedTicketValidator.constructValidationUrl() appends the request-supplied ticket value to the outbound CAS validation URL without URL-encoding, allowing parameter injection into the request sent to the CAS server (e.g. injecting pgtUrl/renew). Rejected as a candidate: the URL host stays the configured CAS prefix, HashMap iteration places the injected content in the ticket parameter, and the attacker manipulating their own validation request appears to gain only their own ticket/assertion; cross-user impact could not be established from the source.
rejected_leads.reason: Impact cross-user not established; influenced parameters affect the attacker's own validation transaction.

rejected_leads.lead: CommonUtils.readAndRespondToProxyReceptorRequest() stores caller-supplied pgtIou/pgtId pairs into the shared PGT storage without source authentication, and common storage implementations are unbounded between clean-ups. Rejected: retrieving a legitimate PGT requires knowing a CAS-server-generated, unguessable IOU within a short window, and the memory-growth angle is a generic DoS rather than a distinct evidenced root cause.
rejected_leads.reason: No feasible path to consume another party's PGT traced; unguessable IOU and short expiry window.

rejected_leads.lead: AbstractEncryptedProxyGrantingTicketStorageImpl uses DESede (ECB, default JCE transformation), no integrity protection, and a lossy byte[]<->String conversion. Rejected: opt-in and configuration-dependent; no attacker-controlled decryption/verification path was traced, and it is primarily a correctness/weak-crypto concern rather than an injectable vulnerability.
rejected_leads.reason: Configuration-gated weak cryptography without a traced attacker-controlled exploit path.

summary: Reviewed the Jasig/apereo java-cas-client 3.3.2-SNAPSHOT source tree (135 Java files; cas-client-core plus Atlassian/JBoss/Tomcat 6/7 integration and distributed-storage modules). The single strongest evidence-supported candidate is a partially hardened XML parser in cas-client-core's XmlUtils, which parses attacker-controllable Single-Sign-Out messages (front-channel SAMLRequest GET and back-channel logoutRequest POST) with only load-external-dtd disabled and without disallow-doctype-decl / external-general-entities=false / external-parameter-entities=false, leaving a plausible XXE (blind file read / SSRF / DoS) exposure. Several other suspicious constructs were reviewed and rejected or downgraded as config-dependent or non-exploitable (listed below). Coverage is static-only; no code was executed and no runtime confirmation was obtained.
